# Siltwake M1 decomposition advice

Date: 2026-10-17. Role: bounded Astra xhigh technical-lead/design advisor. Root remains sole dispatcher, integration owner and acceptance coordinator. This is a source/evidence decomposition audit, not an independent acceptance review. No M1 feature is declared accepted. Only M0 has acceptance, at `d41543694bd68e8e41a01465df7141634a5567f2`.

## Recommendation

Preserve the implementation. Most M1 mechanisms already exist; the remaining job is to close real composition/physical-route gaps, complete final-source ordinary play, and refine the rendered interactions and presentation together. Do not restart inventory, survival, vehicles, recovery, saves or the renderer. Use one main Sol 6.1 max for core/composition, one Sol 6.1 max for visual assets/readability, and one Sol 6.1 max for presentation/story/audio. Rotate a carrier/recovery specialist into a freed slot only for the concrete leaf work described below. No more than three workers plus root.

The most useful immediate main-builder task is a small shared-contract and command/save correctness pass, followed by a bounded production route. It should precede parallel mutation. The existing render/UI interfaces already support exclusive ownership: a large architectural extraction is unnecessary. The second Astra adds value as a short contract/dependency audit between phases, then leaves its slot. It must not become a dispatcher, permanent manager or acceptance reviewer of this advice.

M1-01 remains the full milestone checklist: first linked expedition, early carrier/collision feasibility, recovery and persistent state. The approximately ten-hour main story, optional exploration, six useful craft and both campaign strategies remain later obligations. This proposal neither implements nor reduces those later obligations.

## Bounded dependency-ordered assignments

These are proposed assignments for root to reconcile and dispatch. They do not themselves transfer ownership. All use Sol 6.1 at max, no children. Start each isolated worktree from root's committed provisional baseline; do not copy unfinished builder files. Preserve the existing source history and final evidence commit.

### A0 — Main builder: shared seam and immediate consistency checkpoint

**Prerequisite:** root records the completed handoff and stages the preserved source/evidence on a provisional feature candidate. Not integration acceptance. Main alone edits production during this short prerequisite block.

**Scope:** reconcile schema2/export/physical-coordinate contracts in a proposal to root; fix the immediate command/snapshot issues in risk R1; freeze dimensions/interaction positions and existing render/UI interfaces; resolve the small sound-origin seam in R5. Establish how the carrier launch corridor will be represented and checked before delegating its final art. Return a coherent commit **S** with affected checks. Root updates coordinator-owned CONTRACTS/TASKS and commits that baseline before independent worktrees.

**Smallest necessary extractions:** none for the initial split. Existing `createExpeditionArt(...).update(state)`, `AnimatedLife.update(seconds)`, `GameView` callbacks and `Soundscape` already separate the assigned paths. Keep all of `src/render/expedition.ts` with one visual author; do not carve vehicle art away merely to add a carrier worker. Keep the single registry intact. The presentation author can edit notebook composition and UI prose now; registry text changes return as an exact proposed patch for the main builder to apply serially. This is cheaper and safer than a new content architecture for four clues.

If subsequent actual prose work proves that serial registry edits are a bottleneck, **main first** extracts only non-persistent display copy to `src/content/expedition-copy.ts`, preserves existing assembled registry exports, and commits a new baseline before transferring that one new path. IDs, positions, quantities, unlocks and especially saved `provenance` stay core-owned. Do not do this preemptively. No registry/types/world/save/renderer file receives two owners.

**Interfaces frozen at S:** `GameState/GameCommand`, `WorldQueries`, registry IDs/recipe relationships, `GameRenderer` and availability callback, `UiActions/PanelKind`, `Soundscape` lifecycle, carrier frames and physical envelopes. A minimal optional spatial origin on sound events is sufficient to distinguish directional hunter warnings from body/system alarms; all producers change here first, without adding saved state. If new physical lock geometry is needed, main supplies its authoritative read-only descriptor before dependent visual mutation. No platform/dependency changes are indicated.

**Tests/exit:** affected command → encode/decode tests, app menu/pause composition, migration/ownership, hull/collision and carrier rules; `npm run check` plus production economy checker. Document actual failures and unchanged exports. A0 is part of the core completion batch below, not a separate acceptance ceremony for extraction edits.

## What must stay together

1. **Command/state/save composition:** `executeCommand` can change state while panels stop ticks. `stepGame` advances those same identities through survival, threat, docking and recovery; `validState` validates their relationships; session/repository serialize detached snapshots; app controls pause/entry permission. Splitting their ownership invites states that only become valid after a later tick. Main owns this cluster even if carrier/recovery leaf implementations rotate.
2. **Registry, source positions and world:** `terrainHeight` literally blends terrain around `SOURCES` positions (`world.ts:23`). Source relocation affects collision, node visuals, collection radius, route oxygen and evidence context. Recipes, persistent blueprint keys, cargo output and build clearance are also co-located in the registry. Keep one owner. The design JSON remains comparison input only.
3. **Physical art authority:** terrain/solids/refuge thresholds, hull envelopes, local berth coordinates and launch volumes are a joint contract. Visual detail can vary behind render interfaces; the physical contract cannot vary independently. Keep main's `renderer.ts` lifecycle, camera/readiness, `materials.ts` and `atmosphere.ts` ownership explicit and separate from art leaf files.
4. **Persistent knowledge/provenance:** `discover` adds plans and recorded provenance; save validation reproduces the allowed plan relation and compares provenance text exactly. A prose author cannot rename an ID or provenance string as copyediting. Keep C01–C04 meaning and actual ecology coherent; later reveal content is outside this batch.
5. **Recovery investment and containers:** disabled-vessel identity, original frame investment, fitted retained tools, packed/deployed buoy, caches, bound repairs and save ownership form one conservation system. A leaf tow fix must not invent a second cargo store or turn maintenance allocation into general purchasing materials.

## Concrete high-impact risks and dispositions

Priorities below mean implementation/verification order before M1 completion, not independent acceptance verdicts. Source-derived defect candidates need a focused reproduction by the owner of the affected path.

### R1 — P1: menu commands can expose invalid persistent intermediate state

`carrier.ts:188` handles `helm` by setting `controlledVehicleId` and clearing interior mode/pose, but does not immediately place the player at the carrier's world pose. From `fixtureGame`, the player is at local `(0,4,-6)`, not the hull keel. `SiltwakeApp.command` calls `executeCommand` while a panel is paused; F5/manual save can run before `stepGame` repairs the pose. `validation.ts:602` onward requires piloted player/vehicle positions within 0.01 m. This creates a direct source-derived immediate-save failure candidate. Existing carrier test takes helm, leaves it and/or advances before saving, so its green result does not cover the exact cut.

Also, `recovery.ts:115` field repair clears `disabled` and the loss entry without clearing a same-hull `recovery.operation`; the validator requires an active operation's hull to remain disabled (`validation.ts:697`). Starting local tow, then choosing repair in the same paused panel can expose the inconsistency; `updateRecovery` does not itself reject an already repaired target.

**Disposition:** A0 owns coherent complete command transactions; test command → immediate encode/decode before any tick, plus actual menu/save paths. Include helm, return to interior, repair/cancel/active tow and station-keeping transitions. Do not weaken the validator merely to hide a transient invalid state.

### R2 — P1: one successful rescue fixture does not cover the loss-capable M1 area

`rescueWaypoints` uses one fixed shallow corridor followed by the current hull position; `recoveryCommand` refuses stage distance >230 m (`recovery.ts:185`). Approach movement has no world collision query; tow uses the full Dart footprint and aborts to a local repair/salvage message on obstruction. Both alternatives require local collar access. The world permits deep eastern travel outside the one tested loss `(93,-88,-96)`, with a 150 m suit and 180 m Dart; a blocked tow or loss outside the tether envelope can therefore leave a site where the prescribed fallback is unsafe for the diver. This is a coverage/design risk, not a claim that every such route was reproduced.

**Disposition:** A/D play the intended and adverse reachable loss sites, including depleted power, clearance failure and a second failed recovery. Validate the entire physical path and safe reachable outcome, including the final shallow mooring placement. Adjust authored staging/corridor geometry or usable M1 extent with explicit rationale if necessary. Do not solve it through global summon, an upgraded duplicate vessel or postponing the M1 recovery gate to M2.

### R3 — P1: carrier transaction correctness is ahead of physical launch proof

`launchRefusal` checks `hullClearance` at `launchPoint` and another craft's distance to that point (`carrier.ts:298`). `updateBerth` waits 30 ticks then assigns the endpoint (`:347–365`); capture likewise assigns the berth. It does not sweep a hull through the complete berth/lock/exit corridor. `dartArt`'s Hearthline branch in `render/expedition.ts:21` depicts an open interior/deck; dry isolation is chiefly a state invariant at present. Existing obstruction tests place a solid at the endpoint, not between a clear endpoint and the berth.

**Disposition:** before detailed carrier art, main/D define a simple physical lock route/volume and authoritative compartments sufficient for the specified feasibility fixture, and validate preflight plus commit against it. A fluid solver or a detailed moving-interior system is unnecessary. Test a clear endpoint with an obstructed intervening volume; both compact slots and medium configuration; changing clearance after preparation; actual visible lock/other-berth safety. Keep fixture evidence separate from campaign availability.

### R4 — P1: final hull geometry invalidates assumptions in old route evidence

The final Dart envelope is radius 3.6 / height 2.1; Hearthline 17 / 9.2. `world.ts:hullFloor/hullClearance/moveHull`, `FACILITY_SOLIDS` and registry build pose implement stronger geometry than the earlier full route. Author moved Dart's build z from -24 to -22 and explicitly says the old saved hull pose needs physical rechecking. The schema2 validator checks identities/ranges, not every terrain/collision clearance; successfully decoding an old save is not proof that the imported boat can leave its cradle.

**Disposition:** A replays construction/launch/return on final source, checks old provisional save placement separately, and keeps art dimensions fixed through B. If compatibility repair is needed, preserve the original record and use an explicit content/migration policy. Do not claim the earlier 494.744 m route validates the final shape. Large hull/waterline/narrow-route checks are still necessary.

### R5 — P2, fix at the shared seam: all warnings currently sound spatially like the hunter

`Soundscape.event` pans every `cue === 'warning'` toward `world.threat.position` (`sound.ts:106`). `updateSurvival` emits the same cue for oxygen, food, pressure and power; `GameEvent` has no origin/reason. A low-air alarm away from the encounter can therefore imply a creature direction. The host was muted, so historical runtime work cannot resolve this perceptual issue.

**Disposition:** A0 supplies a minimal sound-origin contract; C pans only actual spatial threat events and keeps body/equipment alarms nonspatial, with matching readable hazard cues. Preserve volume/mute/captions and browser activation. Do not add a new audio dependency.

### R6 — P1 evidence closure: preparation reserve failure and final-route incompleteness

The retained metrics corroborate the older preparation minimum 20.8241%, below the required 25%. Final-source partial preparation is 94.2963%, but excludes several required purchases/legs and all powered travel. `scripts/check-m1-economy.mjs` sums stock/cost and patches; it does not model actual containers, navigation or consumption. `GameState.metrics.minOxygen/minPower` are cumulative and will include later intentional failure, so a single post-failure value cannot establish earlier first-access margins.

**Disposition:** A retains saves/measurements at leg boundaries before the intentional failure branch, including useful cargo, air/power before replenishment, collection/transfer counts and route/time. Fix observed collision/readability/hauling causes before tuning stock. Keep reserves and optional-spending arithmetic reconciled, with no waiting/grind added to fill duration.

### R7 — P2 seam constraint: copy edits can invalidate saves or overstate ecology

`validation.ts:213` requires saved finding provenance to equal current registry text exactly. `discover` also determines plans from clue IDs, while `GameView` presents combined interpretation. Separately, `AnimatedLife.update(seconds)` has no gameplay-state input: its schools orbit prescribed upper-water paths. Current C04 cites the observed distribution and a historical field sheet; this is not proof of a responsive chemistry simulation.

**Disposition:** retain persistent provenance/IDs under A; C changes display prose through the described serial interface only. B/C can make existing flow, grazers and upper/lower distribution legible, but must not claim new behavioral causes without actual core support. No new ecology subsystem is required to satisfy the already-existing filter-flow/grazer relation.

Read-only observations of HUD/save are fine; injected state, stock, teleports or direct simulation calls are diagnostic and must not establish these passes.

Complete any unobserved final-source early order after assembly changes. |

Keep fixture F0–F3 separate from New expedition and its save storage: F0 stationary interior/helm/vestibule and large-hull collision/waterline; F1 both dry compact berths, blocked launch with unchanged identity/cargo/charge/damage, Dart launch while Spindle stays safe, surface-only Spindle; F2 clear both slots through actual controls, reach supported dock, configure one medium, capture/launch with whole-volume clearance; F3 prepared and lock save/reload, deliberate interruption/focus pause, obstruction after preparation, exactly-once detachment and incapacity/refuge fallback. A fixture failure drill is seeded feasibility evidence, not the normal expedition's gameplay failure. Browser briefs must first require reading `/work/repos/fleet/BROWSER_RULES.md` and `docs/BROWSER_RULES.md`, verifying factory-worker/isolated Linux browser ownership, preferring T3 `preview_status` then `preview_open`, and task-owned incognito storage/unique ports. Preserve human/root/author tabs and ports; no owner's Windows desktop automation. Pointer lock only on isolated Linux. Do not touch author port 5188. Close only owned resources. Use short bounded input blocks and recording segments to avoid repeating the reported timeout/lost-recording problem. No hardware/human claims from agent or software-rendered evidence.

## Assembly and review order

1. Root records handoff, inspected SHAs and path release; stages preserved M1 feature source/evidence provisionally. Main finishes A0; root reconciles contracts and commits S before worktrees. No acceptance is implied.
2. Run A/B/C under exclusive ownership. Share proposed seam changes through root and main; dependent work waits for a committed replacement baseline. Root assembles coherent commits on a provisional feature candidate; main validates composition. Related small corrections remain part of their bounded batch.
3. Freeze geometry and rotate D only if the remaining carrier/recovery work warrants it. Root explicitly transfers its three existing files and records baseline F. Otherwise A completes the same checks. Every delivered change has an identified batch/owner.
4. Finish P0–P5 and F0–F3 on the combined source; retain exact final artifacts. Root inspects source, logs and actual rendered/runtime evidence. Do not accept three isolated folders or passing seeded rules as integrated M1.
5. Freeze one feature candidate covering named **core/physical-feasibility** and **first-expedition presentation** completion batches. They may share the same two independent review tasks, provided both reviewers explicitly cover and disposition every delivered piece and its dependencies. Fresh non-author Astra xhigh and separate non-author Sol 6.1 max review the same SHA/spec/evidence independently, in addition to root's self-review. Rotate authors out to fit four slots. This advisor cannot be the independent Astra reviewer of work shaped by this contribution.
6. Root reconciles findings, assigns corrections within ownership, reruns affected checks and sends each fresh review round the new frozen SHA, original brief, prior findings/dispositions and unresolved objections. Both must explicitly accept the same corrected candidate. Do not create review rounds per trivial edit or waive missing playable evidence.
7. Only then integrate accepted feature work into the game integration branch. Verify the assembled milestone and obtain the required fresh independent Astra/Sol **integrated M1** gate. Component/batch acceptance is not milestone acceptance. Root alone handles PRs, durable records and integration; this advisory task creates none.

## Use of a second Astra within four slots

Use it for one question at a time: before S, audit ownership and command/save/geometry interfaces; after a failed physical run, reconcile the specific recovery/lock contract; before feature freeze, check that evidence actually covers the combined scope. Each visit returns a short decision/risk artifact, then ends. It does not manage Sol children, reassign files, poll the builder or duplicate root's whole-game plan. Root alone dispatches and integrates. With root+Astra+main there is room for one specialist; rotate the advisor out before running all three implementation workers. Independent acceptance remains a different non-author pair.
